Implement GitHub issue #29 on Doraval. Isolated worktree. Commit there. Do not push. Do not bump versions. Do not close the issue.

## Issue
https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/29
Parent: https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/26
Blocked by #27 (done on main: 0d0f728).

## What to build
Home and README open like agent-browser: short pitch, then the first loop. A Reader can finish one real `--quick` Review from the README alone.

First loop (this order):
1. `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`
2. `dora review --quick`

## Acceptance
- README is **Reader** voice: one-line what it is, install, then the first loop.
- Home keeps a short pitch. CTAs / example block are that same first loop. No feature grid.
- `dora review --quick` from those instructions produces a real Review (not help-text failure). Run it against this repo or a fixture to prove it.
- JSON, `--ci`, `--deep` are not the first commands shown.

## Voice
Reader = human. Do not mix Runner “you” on README/home.

## Scope
- README.md
- Home page (apps/website/pages/index.astro and/or _home components)
- Do NOT delete /for-agents/ or rewrite installation.mdx (ticket #28)
- Do NOT add the long command catalog (ticket #30). README may keep a short “see docs” after the first loop.
- Do NOT rewrite the shipped skill.

Borrow shape from https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser README top + https://agent-browser.dev/ home Example. Do not copy marketing (“native Rust”, feature grid).

## Verify
- README contains both first-loop strings
- Run `dora review --quick` (or `bun run ./src/cli/index.ts review --quick .`) and confirm it is a Review, not --help

Commit: `docs: first loop on home and README`

## Report
Files, commit hash, worktree needs merge?, output snippet of the --quick review you ran.

doraval (dora)

**doraval** is a context engineering toolkit for coding agents. It scans, 10→reviews, fixes, and remembers agent context — skills, plugins, rules, and decisions — so Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and Grok work on every try instead of burning tokens on context you cannot rely on. [Installing](#installing) · [Building from source](#building-from-source) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Repository layout](#repository-layout) · [Development](#development) · [Contributing](#contributing) · 20→[License](#license) **Learn more about doraval at [doraval.dev](https://doraval.dev)** This repository contains the TypeScript source for the `dora` / `doraval` CLI and the agent skill shipped via `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`. **Pronunciation:** *dor-uh-val* · Doraemon + eval
30→ --- ## Installing ### Skill (recommended first step) Installs the agent skill so coding agents load the Doraval checklist when you edit skills, plugins, rules, or agent config: 40→```sh npx skills add saif-shines/doraval ``` ### CLI Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux, and Windows: ```sh # one-shot (no install) 50→npx @hacksmith/doraval # permanent npm install -g @hacksmith/doraval # macOS brew tap saif-shines/tap && brew trust saif-shines/tap && brew install doraval # Bun bun add -g @hacksmith/doraval 60→ dora --version # same binary as doraval ``` Node ≥ 14.18. Alpine/musl: use Bun. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [installation guide](https://doraval.dev/get-started/installation/). ### First run ```sh 70→npx @hacksmith/doraval # scan this project npx @hacksmith/doraval review . # quality gate ``` ```text $ dora Health ✓ .claude/skills/review valid ✗ .claude/skills/deploy Missing "description" 80→ Next 1. dora fix .claude/skills/deploy 2. dora review --all ``` Read-only scan. No API key. Exit codes: `0` clean · `1` issues · `2` could not run. **Paths:** [Audit my agent context](https://doraval.dev/get-started/audit/) · 90→[Quickstart](https://doraval.dev/get-started/quickstart/) · [Use with your agent](https://doraval.dev/for-agents/) ```sh npx @hacksmith/doraval review --all --quick --ci ``` ## Building from source Requirements: 100→ - **[Bun](https://bun.sh)** ≥ 1.3 - Node ≥ 14.18 for the published binary target ```sh bun install bun run dev -- --help # run CLI from source bun run build # emit bin/doraval.js ``` 110→## Documentation Full documentation: [doraval.dev](https://doraval.dev) | Path | Contents | |------|----------| | [Getting started](https://doraval.dev/get-started/) | Audit vs Quickstart | | [Command reference](https://doraval.dev/commands/) | All flags on one page | | [Use with your agent](https://doraval.dev/for-agents/) | Skill, JSON, exit codes, CI | | [Memory](https://doraval.dev/concepts/memory/) | Principles that stick | 120→| [Review tiers](https://doraval.dev/concepts/review-tiers/) | Structure → heuristics → LLM → sessions | ### Commands | Command | Job | |---------|-----| | `dora` / `scan` | Surfaces, health, contradictions, next actions | | `review` | Quality gate (structure → heuristics → LLM → sessions) | | `fix` | Mechanical fixes (`--yes` / `--dry-run` / `--brief`) | | `new --for` | Scaffold skill, rule, agent, or plugin | 130→| `memory` | Principles; enforce in review; promote to AGENTS.md | | `reconcile` | Cross-agent contradictions → shared AGENTS.md | | `sessions` | List / show recent agent sessions | | `config` | Judge / model / settings | | `bump` | Semver in plugin / marketplace manifests | | `providers` | Packaging/spec matrix | | `update` | Self-update | ```sh dora review . --quick --ci 140→dora fix . --dry-run dora memory add "Never use default exports" --weight 8 dora reconcile --dry-run ``` Shell completions: `dora --completion zsh` (or `bash` / `fish`). ## Repository layout | Path | Contents | 150→|------|----------| | `src/cli/` | citty CLI surface (`dora` / `doraval`) | | `src/core/` | Scan, review, fix, memory, sessions, scaffold | | `src/providers/` | Packaging / provider specs (`dora new`, `dora providers`) | | `skills/doraval/` | Agent skill shipped via `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval` | | `apps/website/` | Docs site ([Blume](https://github.com/saif-shines/blume)) | | `scripts/` | Release, platform packages, publish helpers | | `test/` | Fixtures and CLI tests | | `bin/` | Built CLI entry (`doraval.cjs`) | 160→## Development ```sh bun install bun run dev -- --help # run from source bun test # unit + CLI tests bun run typecheck bun run build # emit bin/doraval.js ``` 170→See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for conventions (ponytail ladder, no version bumps unless releasing). ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License MIT — see [`package.json`](package.json) (`"license": "MIT"`). 180→

1→---
title: Quickstart
description: End-to-end tutorial — install the skill, install the CLI, scan, review, fix, scaffold, and remember principles.
sidebar:
  label: Quickstart
  order: 3
---

**Outcome:** doraval skill installed, `dora` available, project scanned and reviewed, and you know the main commands.
10→
Short path only (skill + review)? Use **[Audit my agent context](/get-started/audit/)** instead.

## What you will do

1. Install the doraval skill  
2. Install the CLI (or keep using `npx`)  
3. Scan the project  
4. Review and fix  
5. Scaffold new context (optional)  
20→6. Record a principle (optional)  

**Time:** about 10–15 minutes. **Needs:** Node (for `npx`), a project with or without agent files.

---

## 1. Install the doraval skill

```bash

30→```

Agents load this checklist when you edit skills, plugins, rules, or agent config. The skill runs the same `dora` engine you use by hand (or `npx @hacksmith/doraval` if `dora` is not on PATH).

<details>
<summary>What if npx skills add fails?</summary>

- Need network and a current Node  
- Retry: `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`  
- List installed skills: `npx skills list`  
40→</details>

---

## 2. Put the CLI on PATH (or use npx)

**One-shot (no install):**

```bash
npx @hacksmith/doraval --version
50→```

**Permanent (pick one):**

```bash
# macOS
brew tap saif-shines/tap && brew trust saif-shines/tap && brew install doraval

# npm
npm install -g @hacksmith/doraval
60→
# Bun
bun add -g @hacksmith/doraval
```

After install, `dora` and `doraval` are the same binary. Verify:

```bash
dora --version
```
70→
<details>
<summary>PATH / Alpine notes</summary>

- Global install but `dora` not found: add your npm/Bun global bin directory to `PATH`  
- Alpine/musl: use Bun (`bunx` / `bun add -g`); platform binaries target glibc  
</details>

Full matrix: [Installation](/get-started/installation/).

80→---

## 3. Scan the project

```bash
dora
# same as: dora scan
# or: npx @hacksmith/doraval
```

90→**Read-only.** No API key. You get:

| Section | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Agent surfaces | Which agents look configured |
| Health | Skill / manifest issues |
| Next | Numbered follow-ups (`dora fix …`, `dora review …`) |

```bash
dora --format json    # for agents / scripts
100→dora --ci             # implies JSON
```

---

## 4. Review quality

```bash
dora review .
dora review ./path/to/skill-dir
110→dora review --all
dora review --quick .              # structure + heuristics only
dora review --all --quick --ci     # CI gate, no LLM
```

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Clean |
| `1` | Issues found |
| `2` | Could not run |
120→
Tiers (structure → heuristics → LLM → sessions): [Review tiers](/concepts/review-tiers/).

---

## 5. Fix mechanical issues

```bash
dora fix .
dora fix --dry-run
130→dora fix --yes                 # agents / CI (no TTY prompt)
dora fix --brief               # prompt for judgment items
```

| Kind | Examples | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mechanical | Frontmatter, paths | Diff first; apply on approval or `--yes` |
| Judgment | Vague descriptions | Not auto-written; use `--brief` then re-review |

Re-run `dora review .` until exit `0`.
140→
---

## 6. Scaffold new context (optional)

```bash
dora new
dora new skill --for claude --name review-pr --description "Reviews PRs" --yes
dora new rule --for cursor --name no-default-exports --yes
dora new plugin --for claude --name my-plugin --yes
150→```

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `skill` | Reusable `SKILL.md` |
| `rule` | Always-on convention |
| `agent` | Subagent role |
| `plugin` | Package to ship |

Always pass `--for <agent>` for non-interactive runs. Then `dora review` the new path.
160→
---

## 7. Record a principle (optional)

```bash
dora memory add "Never use default exports" --weight 8
dora memory list
dora memory promote              # hard rules → AGENTS.md (diff + confirm)
dora memory context --json --quiet   # SessionStart hooks
170→```

Weights: **8+** hard rule · **5** default · **1–3** soft. [Memory concept](/concepts/memory/).

---

## 8. Cross-agent conflicts (when scan reports them)

```bash
dora reconcile --dry-run
180→dora reconcile
# or: dora reconcile --apply --yes
```

Settles contradictions into shared `AGENTS.md`. [dora reconcile](/commands/#reconcile).

---

## Use with your agent

190→After step 1, paste or rely on the skill:

```text
Review my agent context with dora (npx @hacksmith/doraval). Fix mechanical issues with --yes. Do not report done until review exits 0.
```

JSON, exit codes, CI examples: [Use with your agent](/for-agents/).

---

200→## Command map

| Job | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Scan project | `dora` |
| Review | `dora review` |
| Fix | `dora fix` |
| Scaffold | `dora new --for …` |
| Principles | `dora memory` |
| Conflicts | `dora reconcile` |
210→| Sessions | `dora sessions` |
| Config / judge | `dora config` |

Full flags: [Command reference](/commands/).

## Next

- **[Audit my agent context](/get-started/audit/)** — short skill + review path only  
- **[Use with your agent](/for-agents/)** — automation details  
- **[Command reference](/commands/)** — full flags for every command  
220→

description: Install the doraval skill, then run dora review — the short path to check skills, rules, and plugins.

---

**Outcome:** your coding agent has the doraval skill, and you have run a real review on this project.
10→
## 1. Install the doraval skill

```bash
npx skills add saif-shines/doraval
```

This installs the skill into your agent’s skill directory. After this, the agent can load the doraval checklist when you edit skills, plugins, rules, or agent config.

## 2. Review with dora
20→
Same engine the skill uses. No permanent install required:

```bash
# whole project
npx @hacksmith/doraval review .

# one skill directory (folder that contains SKILL.md)
npx @hacksmith/doraval review ./path/to/my-skill

30→# machine-readable (agents / CI)
npx @hacksmith/doraval review . --format json
```

If `dora` is already on PATH (after [Installation](/get-started/installation/)):

```bash
dora review .
dora review ./path/to/my-skill --format json
```
40→
## 3. Read the exit code

| Code | Meaning | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Clean | Done for this pass |
| `1` | Issues found | Fix, then re-run review |
| `2` | Could not run | Fix the blocker (e.g. missing judge for `--deep`) |

**Do not treat the work as finished while the code is `1` or `2`.**
50→

```bash
npx @hacksmith/doraval fix . --dry-run
npx @hacksmith/doraval fix . --yes
npx @hacksmith/doraval review .
```

Judgment items (vague copy, missing guardrails) need a hand edit — `fix --brief` prints a prompt for your agent.
60→

1→# Doraval — domain context

Agent-readable glossary for architecture and code. Product language wins over legacy file names.

## Product

**Doraval** (`dora` / `doraval`) is a context-engineering CLI: scan, review, and manage agent skills, memory files, and rules across Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and Grok.

## Core terms
10→
| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Skill** | A directory with `SKILL.md` (frontmatter + body) that agents load as specialized instructions. |
| **Review** | One `review(path)`. Tiered quality pass over a Skill and/or Memory file: structure → heuristics → optional LLM judge → optional sessions. Workspace and Skill reviews also include cwd Memory files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `copilot-instructions.md`). |
| **Scan** | Fast workspace health check (`dora` bare): agents present, skill validation, shadows/overlaps, install/intelligence. |
| **Rule** | One module (`src/core/rules`). Registry, packages, resolve, stamp, and mutation. CLI only renders and writes config. |
| **Package** | Named enable-set of rules: `recommended` (default), `strict`, `minimal`. |
| **Judge** | One module (`judge()`). Owns mode (**api** / **delegate** / **fail**) and transport. Review passes prompt, schema, and `ci`. |
| **Memory** | Product term for principles, artifacts, and always-on files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, …) under `~/.doraval/memory/` and project roots. |
20→| **Config** | Global product config at `~/.doraval/config.yml`. Code type is still `JournalConfig` (legacy name — not a “journal product”). Holds projects, `eval.*` judge settings, rules, agent command. |
| **Session** | Past agent conversation transcript, normalized via **session adapters** into primitives for evidence and adherence eval. |
| **Finding** | One Skill-check outcome (tier + severity + message + optional rule code / docUrl). The Skill-check module sets `structure` or `heuristics`. Review adds `llm` and `sessions`. Scan presents Skill Findings as health; shadows, overlaps, MCP, budget, and install stay Scan-only. |

## Docs voice

Two addressees. Do not mix them on one surface.

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
30→| **Reader** | The human. “you” on README, install, and `get-started`. |
| **Runner** | The agent that executes `dora`. “you” on the skill and on per-command `--help`. |

The website is mixed. Do not mix the two voices on one page.

**`--help` voice:** top-level / most-common help talks to the **Reader**. Per-command help (`dora review --help`, and the rest) talks to the **Runner**.

**First loop:** `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`, then `dora review --quick` so findings show before JSON, LLM, or CI flags.

**README:** Reader surface. Follows the agent-browser README shape (install → quick start → long pasteable command catalog).
40→

**`llms.txt`:** generated from the site. Fix the pages. Do not hand-write a second index.

_Avoid_: one “you” for both; an agent page that still talks to a human (“use with your agent”); leading with `--format json` before a `--quick` review.

50→

1→# Contributing to doraval

## Setup

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run dev -- --help    # run the CLI from source
```

10→Requires Bun ≥ 1.3.0 (see `engines` in `package.json`).

## Before you send a PR

```bash
bun test           # 615+ tests must pass
bun run typecheck  # baseline has pre-existing errors; don't add new ones
```

CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) runs `bun test` on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The matrix must be green.
20→
## Code philosophy

Read `AGENTS.md` first. It has the ponytail ladder (YAGNI → reuse → stdlib → installed deps → shortest form → minimum code) this codebase is written against. In short:

- Deletion and reuse beat new surface. Don't add an abstraction for one caller.
- Non-trivial logic gets one small test, not a suite.
- Never skip trust-boundary validation, data-loss error paths, or security handling.

## Commits
30→
Conventional Commits style (`fix:`, `feat:`, `docs:`, `chore:`), matching `git log` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Keep the subject under ~70 chars; explain *why* in the body when it isn't obvious from the diff.

## Version bumps

Don't bump the version in a PR. Releases are cut by maintainers via `bun run bump` / `bun run release` (see `WIP.md` for current release status and policy).

## Filing issues

Prefer `dora report` from inside a project using doraval. It drafts a sanitized issue (no env values, no secrets) with the diagnostic payload maintainers need. Manual issues are fine too.
40→
## Website docs

Canonical user docs live in `apps/website/content/` (MDX). Pick one addressee per page: **Reader** (human: README, install, get-started) or **Runner** (the agent that executes `dora`: skill, per-command `--help`). Do not mix them. Terms match `CONTEXT.md`.

When writing or editing them:

1. Follow the style prompt in `apps/website/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` (or load the `docs-writing-style` skill in review mode).
2. Prefer website MDX over `docs/developer-journey.md`. The journey file is product narrative with a command rename map at the top; it is not shipping user docs.
3. Open every page with 1–3 sentences of prose before the first code fence. Command pages need options, common mistakes, and related links.
50→
## Where things live

| Area | Path |
|---|---|
| CLI commands | `src/cli/commands/` |
| Core logic (review, fix, scaffold, memory) | `src/core/` |
| Provider specs (`dora new`, `dora providers`) | `src/providers/` |
| Website / docs | `apps/website/` |
| Docs style prompt | `apps/website/.devex-kit/style-prompt-block.md` |
60→

- One idea per paragraph; short paragraphs (2–4 sentences).
- Every command reference page includes: opener, command signature, options table when flags exist, exit codes when relevant, at least one example, a "Common mistakes" section (2–3 bullets), and Related links.

- Show failure modes in prose (exit codes, missing judge, empty sessions) alongside happy path.

- Ellipsis character (…) only when needed; avoid decorative trailing dots.
- Descriptive link text only: never "click here" or bare "this."

60→- title: short, user-shaped (≤60 chars), sentence case unless it is a command name (`dora review`)
- description: one line ≤160 chars, no em dashes
- sidebar.label: 1–3 words for nav
- sidebar.order: integer when the section orders pages

## 1. Install the doraval skill (first step)
10→
```bash
npx skills add saif-shines/doraval
```

This uses the **skills** CLI to install the doraval skill into your agent’s skill directory. After this, Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, or Grok can load the checklist and run `dora` when you edit skills, plugins, rules, or agent config.

How the skill drives checks: [Use with your agent](/for-agents/).

## 2. Review context on your project
20→
```bash
npx @hacksmith/doraval
# same engine the skill uses; after permanent install: dora
```

**[Review my context](/get-started/quickstart/)** walks through the output.

## 3. Optional — put `dora` on PATH

30→After a permanent install, `dora` and `doraval` are the same binary. Not required if you are fine with `npx @hacksmith/doraval` (the skill falls back to that when `dora` is missing).

### Homebrew (recommended, macOS)

```bash
brew tap saif-shines/tap && brew trust saif-shines/tap && brew install doraval
```

Upgrade later with `brew upgrade doraval` or `dora update`.

40→### npm (cross-platform)

```bash
npm install -g @hacksmith/doraval
```

Ships a prebuilt binary per platform (macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64/arm64, Windows x64). Node ≥ 14.18.

### Bun

50→```bash
bun add -g @hacksmith/doraval
# one-shot:
bunx @hacksmith/doraval
```

### Alpine / musl

Platform binaries target glibc. On Alpine/musl, run from source with Bun:

60→```bash
bunx @hacksmith/doraval
```

## Verify

```bash
# skill (skills CLI)
npx skills list

70→# CLI (after permanent install)
doraval --version
dora --version
```

## Common mistakes

- Skipped step 1: agents will not auto-load the doraval checklist until `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`.
- `npx skills add` fails: need network + a recent Node; retry the same command.
- Global install succeeds but `dora` is missing: ensure your npm/Bun global bin directory is on `PATH`.
80→- Alpine or musl hosts: use Bun (`bunx` / `bun add -g`), not the glibc platform binary.

## Problem Statement

Doraval docs still read as if a human is operating the product by hand. The phrasing, tutorials, and “use with your agent” pages talk to a person about their agent.

The product is a CLI that agents run. Humans read so they can install and decide. The bar is the agent-browser docs: install, a pasteable first loop, then a long command catalog.

Old “for agents” copy still addresses a human. Feature-build notes on the command catalog are not a runbook. Some generated index links are already stale. One published heading must not break: `/get-started/quickstart/#4-review-quality`.

## Solution

Revamp every in-scope surface in one pass so a **Reader** (human) and a **Runner** (the agent that executes `dora`) never share “you” on the same surface.

First loop, in that order:

1. `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`
2. `dora review --quick`

Findings show before JSON, LLM, or CI flags.

The README and the site command catalog follow the agent-browser shape: what it is, installation, quick start, then a long pasteable command catalog. The home page keeps a short pitch and the same first loop. There is no `/for-agents/` page. Skill install lives on the install page. The shipped skill stays a full **Runner** workflow. Top-level `--help` talks to the **Reader**. Per-command `--help` talks to the **Runner**. `llms.txt` stays generated from the site.

This pass is done when those surfaces match the new voice **and** a Reader can finish one real `--quick` Review from the README alone. The protected heading still resolves.

## User Stories

1. As a Reader, I want a one-line “what this is” at the top of the README, so that I know why to install.
2. As a Reader, I want install commands first, so that I can put `dora` on the machine.
3. As a Reader, I want the next block to be `npx skills add saif-shines/doraval`, so that my coding agent can load Doraval.
4. As a Reader, I want the next command to be `dora review --quick`, so that I see Findings before JSON or an LLM wait.
5. As a Reader, I want a long pasteable command catalog on the README, so that I can copy a verb without opening the site.
6. As a Reader, I want the same catalog on the site, so that the docs site and GitHub do not disagree on the command list.
7. As a Reader, I want the site catalog path to follow agent-browser’s pattern, so that the tree feels familiar.
8. As a Reader, I want the home page to keep a short pitch, so that the product still has a face.
9. As a Reader, I want home-page CTAs to be the first loop, so that I do not start in a 15-minute tutorial.
10. As a Reader, I want get-started and install pages to say “you” to me, so that install steps are unambiguous.
11. As a Reader, I want `dora --help` to speak to me, so that the common entry is human-readable.
12. As a Reader, I want `#4-review-quality` on the quickstart to keep working, so that the one published doraval.dev link in the friction log does not 404.
13. As a Reader, I want existing journal/validate redirects to keep working, so that old bookmarks still land.
14. As a Reader, I do not want new redirects for pages we move, so that this pass is not a redirect project.
15. As a Reader, I want `/for-agents/` gone, so that I am not sent to a page that talks about “my agent.”
16. As a Reader, I want skill install on the install page, so that agent setup sits next to CLI install.
17. As a Reader, I want an `AGENTS.md` snippet on the install page, so that I can point my agent at `dora` in one paste.
18. As a Reader, I want get-started to stop saying “what you will do in 10–15 minutes” as the main path, so that the first loop is the first win.
19. As a Reader, I want concepts pages to stay conceptual but drop tutorial “you will,” so that they do not pretend I am in a workshop.
20. As a Reader, I want Rule reference pages to stay lookup pages, so that a Finding’s doc URL still makes sense.

- Two addressees only: **Reader** and **Runner**. One “you” per surface. Do not mix them on one page.
- In-scope surfaces: website, README, shipped skill, generated `llms.txt`, and CLI `--help`.
- First loop is fixed: skill add, then `dora review --quick`. JSON, `--ci`, and `--deep` come after.
- README shape matches agent-browser: one-line product, installation, quick start, long pasteable command catalog. No centered marketing block.
- The site carries the same long catalog. Prefer agent-browser’s catalog path. The path is not sacred.

- Shipped skill stays a full **Runner** document (workflow, JSON, exit codes, no TTY). It must not copy the flag encyclopedia.
- Top-level `--help` is **Reader** voice. Each `dora <command> --help` is **Runner** voice (imperative).
- `llms.txt` remains generated from the site. Fix stale pages so the index is correct. Do not hand-author a second index.

- Product terms stay: Skill, Review, Scan, Rule, Package, Judge, Memory, Config, Session, Finding.

2. README contains the first loop strings (`npx skills add saif-shines/doraval` and `dora review --quick`).

4. The old agent page is absent from the built site (no nav entry, no page).
5. Acceptance (manual or scripted CLI): from the README first loop, `dora review --quick` on a fixture or this repo exits as a real Review (not a help-text failure).

Do not add a new docs-test framework. Prefer the existing site check. Extend it only if a check above cannot be seen there.

- `dora skills get` (later product ticket).
- Completeness pass: one runnable example for every public command (later).
- Redirects for entire.io or other friction-log URLs we do not own.
- New 301s for every moved page.

- Copying agent-browser marketing (feature grid, “native Rust,” token math).

npx skills add saif-shines/doraval
